questions.question_text: A tenant has lived in an Oregon rental unit for 14 months. Under SB 608, what must the landlord have to terminate the tenancy?
distractors: Permission from the local housing authority
questions.explanation: After the first 12 months of occupancy a landlord needs cause to terminate (ORS 90.427). Inside the first year a month-to-month tenancy can still be ended with 30 days' notice and no reason at all.

questions.question_text: Which is an at-fault cause allowing a landlord to terminate under Oregon's just-cause requirement?
questions.correct_answer: Repeated lease violations by the tenant
distractors: Owner plans to move into the unit
Sale to a buyer who will occupy
questions.explanation: At-fault causes are tenant conduct: nonpayment, lease violations, criminal activity. Owner or family occupancy, an accepted offer from a buyer who will occupy, unsafe repairs, and demolition or conversion are qualifying landlord reasons with their own notice and payment rules.

questions.question_text: An Oregon landlord terminates a tenancy for a no-fault reason after 12 months of occupancy. What must the landlord provide?
questions.correct_answer: 90-day notice and one month's rent relocation
questions.explanation: A qualifying landlord reason after the first year — demolition or conversion, unsafe repairs, landlord or family occupancy, or an accepted offer from an occupying buyer — needs 90 days' notice plus one month's rent. Landlords with four or fewer units owe no payment (ORS 90.427).

questions.question_text: An Oregon tenant gives written notice of a leaky faucet and the landlord does nothing. What may the tenant do under ORLTA?
questions.correct_answer: Repair it and deduct up to $300 from rent
distractors: Repair it and deduct up to one month's rent
Withhold all rent until it is fixed
questions.explanation: For a minor habitability defect — one repairable for $300 or less — a tenant who gives written notice and waits the statutory period may have it fixed and deduct the actual, reasonable cost up to $300 (ORS 90.368).

questions.question_text: Under ORLTA, which tenant remedy allows a court to order a landlord to make specific repairs?
questions.explanation: Injunctive relief is a court order compelling the landlord to perform specific actions such as making repairs. This is one of three main remedies available to Oregon tenants alongside repair-and-deduct and lease termination.

questions.question_text: Oregon became the first state in the nation to enact statewide rent control through which law?
questions.explanation: SB 608 (2019) made Oregon the first state in the nation to pass statewide rent control, capping annual rent increases at 7% plus the consumer price index.

questions.question_text: Under SB 611 (2023), what is the hard cap on annual rent increases in Oregon regardless of CPI?
questions.explanation: SB 611 (2023) capped annual increases at the lesser of 10 percent or 7 percent plus CPI. The Department of Administrative Services publishes the figure by September 30 each year; for 2026 it is 9.5 percent (ORS 90.324).

questions.question_text: A landlord owns a rental home built 8 years ago. Is the property subject to Oregon's statewide rent control cap?
questions.correct_answer: No, properties under 15 years old are exempt
distractors: Yes, all rental properties are covered
Only if the unit is in a city over 50,000
Only if the landlord owns three or more units
questions.explanation: The cap applies only once the dwelling's first certificate of occupancy is at least 15 years old (ORS 90.323). Newer construction is exempt to encourage building, and the test is the building's age, not how long the landlord has owned it.

questions.question_text: A manufactured dwelling park with 40 spaces plans a rent increase. What annual cap applies under Oregon law?
questions.explanation: Manufactured dwelling and floating home facilities with more than 30 spaces are capped at 6 percent a year, below the general formula; facilities with 30 or fewer follow the lesser of 10 percent or 7 percent plus CPI (ORS 90.324, HB 3054 of 2025).

questions.question_text: How much advance notice must an Oregon landlord provide before raising rent on a covered unit?
questions.explanation: A landlord must give at least 90 days' written notice before a rent increase, and may not raise rent at all during the first year of a tenancy (ORS 90.323). The notice has to state the new rent and the effective date.

questions.question_text: Oregon law sets the maximum security deposit a landlord may collect at:
questions.correct_answer: No statutory cap on the deposit amount
distractors: One month of the tenant's rent
Two months of the tenant's rent
First and last month's rent combined
questions.explanation: Oregon sets no dollar cap on a security deposit, but it does restrict changes: no new or increased deposit during the first year, and after that the landlord must give the tenant at least three months to pay the increase (ORS 90.300).

questions.question_text: A tenant vacates an Oregon rental on March 1. By what date must the landlord return the security deposit with an itemized statement?
questions.explanation: The landlord has 31 days after the tenancy terminates and the tenant delivers possession to return the deposit or provide a written itemized accounting (ORS 90.300). From a March 1 move-out that is April 1.

questions.question_text: An Oregon landlord willfully withholds $800 of a tenant's security deposit without justification. What penalty may the tenant recover?
questions.explanation: A landlord who withholds a deposit in bad faith, or who skips the written accounting, owes the tenant twice the amount withheld (ORS 90.300). That is on top of returning what was actually due.

questions.question_text: For which of the following may an Oregon landlord lawfully deduct from a security deposit?
questions.correct_answer: Damage beyond normal wear and tear
questions.explanation: Landlords may deduct for unpaid rent, damage beyond normal wear and tear, and cleaning costs if specified in the rental agreement. Normal wear and tear, such as minor scuffs or aged carpet, is not deductible.

questions.question_text: A manufactured dwelling park with 50 spaces plans to close permanently. How much notice must the park owner give residents?
questions.explanation: A facility owner must give residents 365 days' written notice before closing the park (ORS 90.645). Rent increase and just cause protections keep running through the notice period.
